question: In which of the following groups do all the hydrocarbons NOT belong to the same homologous series?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₆**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1: CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₆** - Methane (CH₄) and Ethane (C₂H₆) belong to the alkane series (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂), while Propene (C₃H₆) belongs to the alkene series (CₙH₂ₙ).
 
• **Option 2: C₃H₆, C₅H₁₀, C₇H₁₄** - All these hydrocarbons belong to the alkene series (CₙH₂ₙ).
 
• **Option 3: C₂H₄, C₃H₆, C₄H₈** - All three follow the general formula for alkenes (CₙH₂ₙ).
 
• **Option 4: C₂H₂, C₃H₄, C₄H₆** - All these hydrocarbons belong to the alkyne series (CnH2n-2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A homologous series is a group of organic compounds with a similar general formula, possessing similar chemical properties due to the presence of the same functional group.
 
• Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes have CₙH₂ₙ, and alkynes have CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
 
• Understanding the homologous series helps in predicting the properties and reactions of organic compounds.
